chunks: I said nought to them but what You commanded me: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord. And so long as I dwelt with them I was witness over their actions. And after my life had been done, You were their keeper; and You are a witness over all things.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say he conveyed to the people according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) final testimony on the Day of Judgment, affirming that he fulfilled his duty of *tabligh* (conveyance) without adding or subtracting from the divine message. It underscores the transition of authority from the Prophet's earthly witness to God's ultimate surveillance, reinforcing the concept of *ismah* (infallibility) in the transmission of revelation. The verse serves as a reassurance to the believers that the messenger was accountable only for delivering the truth, while God remains the all-encompassing witness over all creation.
